Hi everyone! Together with two friends @Yusuf Demir and @Yağız Kaan Aydoğdu , we have been working on formalizing quantifier elimination in model theory as our bachelors project.

As part of this, we proved that dense linear orders without endpoints have quantifier elimination. We are planning to open a PR to mathlib soon. The development is currently at https://github.com/BOUN-MATH490/mathlib4. We would be very happy to get feedback on whether the coverage and approach looks suitable for mathlib.

Hello! This is the diff, right?
Note that some of your proofs are very long (e.g. isQFEquivalent_iff_realize_iff_of_embeddings is more than 150 lines, there are two theorems with 70 lines, and many theorems with 30 lines), so perhaps you should split them up first into sensible pieces.
Yes, that’s the diff. Thanks for taking a look! We’ll take care of it and try to split the long proofs into smaller pieces.

We have revised our work to shorten the proofs as much as possible, either by splitting bidirectional proofs or by formalizing repeating logic into new theorems. Some proofs can still be considered lengthy, but the longest one has been reduced from over 150 lines to ~60 lines.

This is quite impressive! Looks like you have the theorem to reduce QE to single exists case, do you further reduce to a disjunction normal form in the proof for DLO? (I will definitely take a deeper look when I have time)

Thanks! In the current formalization, we do not reduce the DLO case to an explicit disjunctive normal form.

We do formalize the general reduction of QE to eliminating one existential quantifier from a quantifier-free formula, which is used as part of the general machinery. But for DLO itself, we prove QE through a model-theoretic extension-pair criterion.

So the proof is more semantic than syntactic. A DNF-based proof for DLO should also be possible, but our aim was to build reusable QE machinery, with DLO as an application. A natural future application would be another classical QE example such as divisible ordered abelian groups. We have not done this yet; as far as I know, the corresponding first-order theory is not currently formalized in mathlib.

Is there any plan to do real closed fields? I might have a crack.
@Michail Karatarakis is trying to get Claude to do it but it's been going for a few days and it's still not got there.

Our current focus is to make the current prs pass, but would love to work on other qe theories afterwards
.
